what_its_for: Fluphenazine decanoate is used to treat schizophrenia and other serious mental health conditions. It helps reduce symptoms like hallucinations (seeing or hearing things that are not there), delusions (false beliefs), and disorganized thinking. It is a long-acting injectable medicine, meaning you do not have to take a pill every day.
how_to_take: This medicine is given as a shot (injection) into your muscle or just under your skin, usually in the buttocks or upper thigh. A healthcare provider such as a nurse or doctor will give you this injection. You will not give this shot to yourself at home. Injections are typically given every 2 to 4 weeks, depending on what your doctor prescribes. Always attend your scheduled appointments to make sure you receive your doses on time.
dosing: The dose is different for each person and is decided by your doctor based on your symptoms, your body's response to the medicine, and your medical history. A common starting dose for adults is 12.5 mg to 25 mg given every 2 to 4 weeks. Your doctor may slowly adjust your dose up or down to find the best amount for you. Never try to change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss or are late for a scheduled injection appointment, contact your doctor or clinic right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Missing doses can cause your symptoms to return or get worse. Try to keep all of your appointments. If you are not sure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance.
storage: This medicine is stored and handled by your healthcare provider or pharmacy. If you are told to store it at home for any reason, keep it at room temperature, away from heat, light, and moisture. Keep it out of reach of children and pets. Do not freeze this medicine. Ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of any unused medication.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while using this medicine, as it can increase drowsiness and dizziness and may make side effects worse. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, because it can cause drowsiness and slowed reactions. Avoid getting too hot or overheating, since this medicine can reduce your body's ability to regulate temperature. Be careful in very hot weather or during strenuous exercise. Avoid standing up too quickly, as this medicine can cause a drop in blood pressure and make you feel dizzy or faint. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, because many drugs can interact with fluphenazine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: stiff muscles, high fever, confusion, or sweating (these could be signs of a rare but serious condition called neuroleptic malignant syndrome); uncontrolled muscle movements in your face, tongue, or body that you cannot stop (this may be a condition called tardive dyskinesia); severe restlessness or the feeling that you cannot stay still; difficulty swallowing or breathing; irregular or fast heartbeat; seizures; yellowing of your skin or eyes; or thoughts of harming yourself. Also call your doctor if your mental health symptoms get worse or if you develop any new, bothersome side effects.
when_it_works: Fluphenazine decanoate does not work immediately. Some improvement in symptoms may be noticed within the first few days to weeks after starting treatment, but it often takes several weeks to months to feel the full benefit of this medicine. It is very important to continue receiving your injections as scheduled, even if you feel better. Stopping the medicine suddenly can cause your symptoms to return. Talk to your doctor before making any changes to your treatment.
special_populations: Older adults: Elderly patients, especially those with dementia, may have a higher risk of serious side effects including stroke or death. This medicine is not approved for treating dementia-related behavior problems. Older adults are also more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness and falls. Pregnancy: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Babies born to mothers who used this medicine during pregnancy may experience muscle problems or withdrawal symptoms after birth. Breastfeeding: This medicine may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Children: Safety and effectiveness in children has not been well established. Discuss with your doctor if this medicine is appropriate. Kidney or liver problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
